prompt:
A 50 nm gold film is evaporated on a glass slide (n = 1.5). In our setup the 633 nm beam comes in through the glass and hits the gold from the glass side, at normal incidence; the other side of the gold is air. What reflectance do we measure on the glass side? (Ignore the back surface of the slide, J&C gold.)

---
Report your result by calling submit_answer with these values:
- `reflectance` (fraction (0-1)): reflectance at 633 nm on the glass side

concerns: The back surface of the slide is ignored, as you asked: the glass is treated as a semi-infinite medium on the incidence side. In practice the uncoated back face (air–glass) reflects about 4% and would add to the signal unless you remove it, e.g. with index matching or a wedged slide.

The gold is modelled as a smooth, uniform 50 nm film with bulk Johnson & Christy optical constants. Real evaporated films can differ (roughness, grain boundaries, an adhesion layer such as Cr or Ti), which can lower the reflectance by a few percent. Any adhesion layer would sit between the glass and the gold, right where the beam enters the gold, so its effect on this measurement could be large.
answer.summary:
The reflectance on the glass side at 633 nm is about **R ≈ 0.863 (86.3%)**.

I set this up as a coherent thin-film (transfer-matrix) calculation: glass (n = 1.5) on the incoming side, then 50 nm of gold with Johnson & Christy optical constants, then air, at normal incidence. The same calculation gives about 4.9% transmitted into the air and about 8.8% absorbed in the gold. These add up to 100%, and the solver gave no warnings. At normal incidence the result is the same for any polarization.

result.conventions:
Lightsmith conventions (fixed; changing them needs a schema version bump):
- Lengths in nm. Wavelengths are vacuum wavelengths in nm.
- Time dependence exp(-i omega t): absorbing materials have Im(eps) > 0 and Im(n) > 0.
- Cross sections in nm^2; efficiencies Q = C / (pi r_eq^2), r_eq = volume-equivalent radius of all particles.
- layer_stack / periodic: layers listed from the superstrate (incidence side) to the substrate; light travels +z.
  R is measured in the superstrate, T in the substrate.
- mode: cross-section in the xy plane, propagation along +z.
- device: ports are planes whose normal is the axis where size_nm is zero; direction is into the device.
- problem.options[<method or backend name>] holds solver options, validated by that backend.
- Materials: {"kind": "constant_index", "n_real": .., "n_imag": ..}, {"kind": "library", "name": "Au"},
  drude, drude_lorentz, tabulated, constant_permittivity. FDTD needs dispersive models (fit_drude_lorentz).
- Results carry provenance and warnings: read the warnings before trusting the numbers.
